facts.t: The Attorney General may sit in Parliament but cannot vote
facts.d: Article 88 lets the AG speak in either House, address joint sittings and take part in committee proceedings — a law officer with the floor of the legislature and no ballot. No other constitutional functionary occupies that position.

facts.t: The AG's salary is not charged on the Consolidated Fund
facts.d: Unlike judges, the CAG or the Election Commissioners, the Attorney General's remuneration is fixed by the government of the day. The financial insulation that protects other constitutional offices simply does not extend here.

facts.t: The Attorney General may keep private clients
facts.d: Private practice is permitted, subject to not appearing against the Union. The office is therefore part-time by design — one of the strongest arguments for making it full-time with commensurate compensation.

bank.q: The Attorney General of India is provided for under:
bank.e: Article 76. Article 88 gives the AG the right to speak in Parliament and Article 143 concerns presidential references to the Supreme Court.

bank.q: With reference to the office of Attorney General, consider the following statements:
s: The holder must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.
The office is held during the pleasure of the President.
There is a fixed tenure of five years.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. There is no fixed tenure at all, which is central to the criticism of the office's independence.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a limitation on the Attorney General?
o: Cannot practise against the Government of India
Cannot appear where the Government is an adverse party
Cannot defend an accused in a criminal case without government consent
bank.e: The AG may participate in the proceedings of either House and give legal clarifications on the floor — though without a vote.

bank.as: The Attorney General's independence is questioned.
bank.rs: The office is held during pleasure, has no fixed tenure, and its remuneration is set by the government rather than charged on the Consolidated Fund.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — three separate structural dependencies, all pointing the same way.

bank.q: Consider the following functions of the Attorney General:
s: Advising the Government of India on legal matters.
Supervising the Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General.
Deciding references made by the President under Article 143.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 143 references go to the Supreme Court, not to the Attorney General.

bank.q: Which episode is most often cited in criticising the AG's independence?
o: The defence of the Aadhaar Act as a Money Bill
bank.e: The 2016 defence of Aadhaar's certification as a Money Bill — cited as prioritising the government's position over constitutional correctness.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed reforms for the office EXCEPT:
o: A statutory framework defining duties and conflict-of-interest rules
Making the office full-time and barring private practice
Making the Attorney General a voting member of Parliament
bank.e: No proposal seeks a vote — that would make a law officer a legislator. The reforms focus on independence, ethics and capacity.

bank.q: Which consultative model is proposed for appointing the Attorney General?
o: Appointment by the Chief Justice alone
A collegium-like mechanism involving the Prime Minister, Chief Justice and Leader of the Opposition
Election by both Houses of Parliament
Selection by the Bar Council of India
bank.e: A tripartite consultative mechanism, mirroring the design used for other independent constitutional appointments.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the importance of the office:
s: It is described as a bridge institution across all three organs of the State.
It provides institutional memory amid changing political leadership.
It is bound by a statutory code of conduct.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. There is no statutory code — unlike the position of British ministers under the Ministerial Code.

bank.q: The Attorney General's heavy litigation load is chiefly attributed to:
o: The government being the largest litigant in India
Mandatory appearance in all High Courts
bank.e: The State is a party in about half of all pending cases — which is why implementing the National Litigation Policy features among the reforms.
